source.title: Towards Guided Descent: Optimization Algorithms for Training Neural Networks At Scale

record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizer outcomes on held-out test accuracy in its own CIFAR-10 experiment, a different setup from the claim versions' specified benchmarks.
record.gate_note: The optimizer comparison in Section 6 bears on V4. Other optimizer and generalization results are cited summaries of prior work and are not extracted as this study's own findings. Batch size is varied in Figure 17, but the text does not state its results.
record.test_reason: The study cites evidence for V4, but its own readable results do not establish Adam's held-out performance relative to SGD. Both are described as suboptimal relative to curvature-aware methods. SPlus overfitting does not establish that comparison either. No other version is tested by the recoverable results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the local experiment's broad message, but overstates the specificity of the reported gap: the prose describes Adam and SGD as suboptimal relative to curvature-aware optimizers without separately quantifying their held-out performance. SPlus exhibits late-training overfitting, and Shampoo fails to converge. The authors present these small experiments as accessible demonstrations of optimization literature, not definitive evidence about generalization across workloads.
record.recipe_differences: The experiment uses a downsampled CIFAR-10 dataset and a 3-layer MLP; it does not test the claim's specified image, language, or random-label settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer and training epoch; SPlus is reported to overfit near the end of training.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam and SGD both exhibit a qualitative suboptimality gap relative to curvature-aware optimizers in the projected-CIFAR-10 MLP experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects training and predictive performance in small MLPs trained on randomly projected image inputs.

fits_no_version.finding: SPlus reduces training loss aggressively and exhibits late-training overfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aggressive optimization with SPlus can produce late-training overfitting in this small-MLP setting.

record.problems: The experiment uses modest 3-layer MLPs and downsampled CIFAR-10. The authors acknowledge limited compute and that more extensive datasets and tuning could have been used. Optimizer-specific test values are shown in figures but not stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 14 contains plotted train-loss and test-accuracy results without numerical values in the supplied text, so no figure-only rows were reconstructed. Figure 17 varies hidden dimension, learning rate, and batch size, but the text reports only aggregate performance and does not state separate outcomes by batch size or width.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error; varying width alone does not establish this.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
A recoverable adaptive-versus-SGD held-out comparison, including its dependence on tuning budget, training performance, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under a fixed epoch budget and whether recipe adaptations remove a penalty.
Controlled dropout comparisons and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy loss.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 14 could potentially establish an Adam-versus-SGD comparison, but its curves are unavailable in the supplied text and are already declared in rows_left_out. Figure 17's width and batch-size sweeps are likewise declared and have no recoverable condition-specific outcomes. Test loss was used for hyperparameter selection, so reported test performance is subject to selection bias. Broader tuning alone would not exclude a result from V4; the decisive issue here is the missing relative comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures on image tasks.

Whether adaptive methods have worse held-out performance than SGD under limited tuning; the study describes its optimizers as heavily tuned and gives no recoverable optimizer-specific test-error values in the text.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the test-accuracy effect.
